A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same SWAP research. All 34 pages of v1 and 33 pages of v2, including figures, equations, tables and appendices, support comparison. Relocated material can be matched reliably.

before.justification: V1 reports original benchmark evaluations, component ablations, search-width/depth analyses and detailed MATH results in Section 4 and the appendices.

after.justification: V2 retains original evaluations and adds Mistral-based experiments, PRM comparisons and a measured token-efficiency study in Appendix F.

M1.justification: The reported inference procedure expands from selecting one plan and returning its controller output in v1 Section 3.1 to retaining b candidate contexts and ranking completed answers in v2 Algorithms 1–2. V2 also introduces structural verification during annotation and inference, including dependency, cycle and redundancy checks. The underlying generator-discriminator architecture, DBM and CR remain.

E1.justification: The represented benchmark coverage remains mathematical reasoning on GSM8K/MATH, logical reasoning on FOLIO/ReClor, and coding on HumanEval/MBPP. The additional backbone, PRM supervision variants and GSM8K efficiency study do not establish a new task, domain, population or test scenario.

E2.justification: Table 1 adds PRM baselines using filtered PRM800K and Math-Shepherd, distinct from the retained PRM-instead-of-CR ablation. It removes GoT and numerous specialist, larger and proprietary model comparisons, including CodeLLaMA, OpenMath, DeepSeekMath, EURUS and GPT models. Self-consistency's coding comparisons are also removed.

E3.justification: V2 adds systematic SWAP and baseline evaluation with Mistral-7B-Instruct and introduces average generated-token usage as an evaluation metric. V1's stated equal search widths for self-consistency and planning are replaced by eight self-consistency/PRM candidates versus five generations per planning step. Newly specified step and breadth limits do not independently establish that retained experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: Appendix F adds an efficiency-performance analysis comparing token consumption on GSM8K. The component ablations, search-width/depth sensitivity analyses and fine-grained MATH analyses are retained, with unchanged corresponding results.

E5.justification: V2 adds ± quantities throughout Table 1, including for retained point estimates that had no uncertainty values there in v1. Their statistical meaning and the underlying run counts or seeds are unspecified. The existing uncertainty bands in the search plots remain unchanged.

E6.justification: Table 1 adds extensive Mistral and PRM results and removes the discontinued comparisons. LLaMA3 zero-shot CoT's HumanEval/MBPP entries change from 50.2/48.8 to 53.3/51.8, without an explained cause. SWAP's original LLaMA3 scores and Tables 2–4 remain unchanged. New Table 5 reports 3612.0 average tokens for SWAP, versus 2214.7 for ToT and 5241.4 for RAP.

T1.justification: V2 Equation 1 explicitly defines the semantic-equivalence distribution by averaging over previous generations. Appendix F adds asymptotic complexity comparisons for SWAP, RAP and ToT. The MDP, entailment-graph definition and DBM normalization are retained; no new correctness theorem or proof is supplied.

C1.justification: The abstract replaces superiority over existing LLMs of similar sizes with superiority over existing methods. The main-results claim likewise shifts away from specialist-model comparisons toward reasoning strategies. The three central contributions and the conclusion's principal claims remain.

C2.justification: V2 replaces the specialist-model-versus-planning interpretation with discussion of intermediate search versus one-pass CoT and PRM verification. It adds a rationale for DBM normalization over softmax. Appendix F explains SWAP's greater token use than ToT through world modeling and graph construction, and its lower use than RAP through fewer simulations.

D1.justification: Appendix D newly reports generator, semantic-equivalence and discriminator training-data counts for every benchmark, plus alternative-sampling details. For MATH these are 49.3k trajectories, 24.2k pairs and 98.2k discriminator trajectories. Search limits and graph-check implementation information are also supplied. These disclosures do not establish increases in previously used training data.

R1.justification: Related work is substantially refocused: broad discussions of retrieval, symbolic reasoning and knowledge-graph applications are removed, while ORM/PRM distinctions and automatic ranking receive expanded positioning. V2 adds explicit DBM comparisons with Vijayakumar et al. (2016) and Hu et al. (2023), and cites additional automatic-supervision work.

P1.justification: The method exposition is substantially rewritten around explicit model conditioning and two algorithms. Related work moves before the preliminaries and is reorganized. Meta-knowledge material moves into a new methodological appendix, and several contrastive-supervision examples are shortened from three candidates to two.

P2.justification: Figure 1 is redrawn to show successive graph construction and candidate branches; DBM and annotation diagrams are revised. Two algorithm blocks and efficiency Table 5 are added. Table 1 is redesigned around two base models with ± entries. The original workflow diagram moves from Figure 2 to appendix Figure 6.

improvement.justification: V2 substantially improves methodological transparency and assessment of the framework: algorithms and training-corpus counts address v1's sparse procedural documentation, while PRM comparisons, a second backbone and measured token costs strengthen empirical scrutiny. Removed cross-model and GoT comparisons reduce breadth. Undefined ± statistics and remaining ambiguity between state-based method notation and history-based appendix prompts limit reproducibility, but the gains in documentation and effectiveness-cost evidence are substantial.
